title: Markup That Stays in the Stream
author: The markwrite authors

abstract.p: A word processor usually keeps a tree of its document and writes the markup out of it when the file is saved. This paper describes the other arrangement, in which the markup is kept in the character stream as the writer typed it and everything else is derived from it, and shows that the arrangement is what lets one editor read seven notations and let a keystroke cost what its paragraph costs.

h1: The stream and the ranges over it
p: A document is a stream of characters and a set of ranges over it. A range has a name and attributes, and covers a stretch of the stream; a token is a range over the characters that represent a piece of markup, and an element is a range derived from the tokens that open and close it. The derivation is the codec's own. XML pairs an opening tag with its closing tag; Markdown pairs a heading's marker with the end of its line; roff pairs a request line with the next request that ends what it began.

Nothing derivable is stored. There is no tree, no role on a range, and no ordinal read off the markup; the point index answers which elements cover a position, and the resolver answers what a style makes of them.

An edit is a replacement of one stretch of the stream by another. Every range past the edit moves by the difference in length, which is one number recorded once rather than a write into every range that moved. The tokens inside the edit are read again by the codec, over a window that begins where the codec knows its state and ends where the tokens it reads fall back into step with the tokens that stood, and only what the window read is dropped and put on again. Everything keyed by a token's identity, the measured widths, the shaped lines, the resolved styles, stays warm.

Where the window cannot be bounded the whole document is read, and the reading says so. A definition in Markdown that every other block reads, a delim line in eqn that every later line reads, and the previous face that roff brings back with \fP are each read whole, since a window cannot know what stands outside it.

Measured on a book of six hundred thousand characters, a keystroke in the middle of a paragraph mutates the model in under seven milliseconds at the ninety-ninth percentile, against sixty-three for reading the whole book again. The frame the keystroke lands in is bounded by the paragraph re-shaped, not the document.

A formula is read into one tree whatever it was written in, and what sets a formula never learns which. MathML is elements and is walked as they stand; TeX and eqn are text and are read by a reader each. So
equation: x sup 2 over y = sqrt {a + b}
p: is the same tree as its TeX, and sets the same.
li: The reader for eqn shares the TeX reader's tables of symbols and function names rather than carrying its own.
A formula in running text stands between the delimiters a delim line sets, and each such run is an inline element the reader reads.

pre.equation: sum from i=1 to n x sub i

p: Keeping the markup in the stream makes the document what the writer wrote, makes the codec a range constructor rather than a parser that owns the document, and makes an edit local. The rest of the editor is what one can build on that.

footnote.p: The sample corpus carries this paper in five notations, the others written from this one by the codecs.
